quick: Neonates (<1 month): 0.05 mL intradermally; Infants >=1 month: 0.1 mL intradermally into left deltoid
STRICTLY INTRADERMAL into left upper arm (deltoid insertion) using 26G/27G tuberculin syringe
Congenital or acquired immunodeficiency, symptomatic HIV infection, generalized eczema/dermatitis
Papule at 2-3 wk -> ulcer/pustule at 5-6 wk -> heals with permanent scar by 8-12 wk; do NOT apply ointments or band-aids
70-80% efficacy against severe forms of childhood TB (tuberculous meningitis, miliary TB); variable protection against adult pulmonary TB
Inspect for regional suppurative lymphadenitis (BCG-itis); observe scar formation
summary: BCG (Bacillus Calmette-Guérin) is a live attenuated strain of Mycobacterium bovis developed for active immunization against tuberculosis. When administered at birth or in early infancy, it confers 70% to 80% protection against the most fatal childhood manifestations of tuberculosis, specifically tuberculous meningitis and disseminated/miliary TB. Administered strictly intradermally at the insertion of the left deltoid muscle. Because it is a live bacterial vaccine, it is absolutely contraindicated in individuals with significant cellular immunodeficiency, including symptomatic HIV infection.
indications: Universal neonatal active immunization at birth (or as early as possible in the first year of life) in high-incidence TB countries (India, WHO policy)
Immunization of tuberculin skin test (TST)-negative or IGRA-negative infants and young children in high-risk households
Intravesical BCG for the adjuvant immunotherapy of non-muscle-invasive bladder cancer (separate clinical formulation and dosage)

dosage.d: 0.05 mL intradermally as a single dose
dosage.t: At birth (or first contact before 1 month)
dosage.n: Reduced volume (0.05 mL) prevents subcutaneous extravasation and severe local abscesses in tiny neonates.

dosage.c: Infants and children (>=1 month of age)
dosage.d: 0.1 mL intradermally as a single dose
dosage.t: Single dose up to 1 year of age
dosage.n: In children >1 year without prior BCG scar, administer only after confirming negative tuberculin skin test (TST/Mantoux).

admin: Reconstitute freeze-dried vaccine strictly with the supplied cold sterile normal saline diluent. Use within 4 hours of reconstitution; keep on ice/refrigerated and protect from direct light.
Administer STRICTLY INTRADERMAL into the skin overlying the insertion of the left deltoid muscle using a fine 26-gauge or 27-gauge short-bevel tuberculin syringe.
A pale, blanched wheal with peau d'orange appearance (5-8 mm diameter) must appear immediately upon correct intradermal injection.
NEVER inject subcutaneously: accidental subcutaneous injection causes severe local cold abscesses, lupoid reactions, and extensive suppurative lymphadenitis.

Advise mothers and caregivers that a small papule will appear in 2-3 weeks, ulcerate, discharge, and heal leaving a permanent scar by 12 weeks. NEVER apply antiseptics, bandages, or ointments to the ulcer.
moa: Viable attenuated Mycobacterium bovis organisms replicate locally within dermal macrophages and drain to regional lymph nodes, triggering a potent Th1 cell-mediated delayed-type hypersensitivity (DTH) response. Activated antigen-specific CD4+ and CD8+ T lymphocytes secrete IFN-gamma, TNF-alpha, and IL-12, activating tissue macrophages to form protective granulomas that arrest hematogenous dissemination of virulent Mycobacterium tuberculosis.

absolute: Severe combined immunodeficiency (SCID) or known primary cell-mediated immunodeficiency

Infants born to HIV-positive mothers who are symptomatic or have confirmed HIV infection (asymptomatic HIV-exposed neonates in high TB burden areas receive BCG per national guidelines if virological testing is negative)
Patients receiving high-dose systemic immunosuppressive therapy, chemotherapy, or biologic anti-TNF agents
relative: Generalized infected eczema, burns, or extensive infectious dermatitis (defer until skin integrity restored)
Acute severe illness or prematurity / birth weight <2000 g (defer until stabilized and gaining weight)
monitor: Disseminated BCG disease (BCG-osis, life-threatening in unrecognized cellular immunodeficiency)

lact: Not indicated for postpartum women; no harm to nursing infant if mother received BCG historically.
common_se: Normal local progression: erythema, papule (2-3 wk), ulceration (5-6 wk), crusting, and permanent scar (8-12 wk)
Mild non-suppurative ipsilateral axillary lymphadenopathy (<1 cm, self-limiting)
serious_se: Suppurative regional lymphadenitis / cold abscess (typically from inadvertent subcutaneous injection)
Disseminated BCG infection / BCG-osis (rare, >95% occurs in infants with severe unrecognized immunodeficiency)
Osteomyelitis / osteitis (extremely rare, 1-5 per million doses)
Keloid scar formation at the injection site
monitoring: Check for presence of typical BCG scar at 3 months of age during subsequent routine vaccination visits
Monitor for persistent, enlarging (>1.5 cm) or fluctuant lymphadenitis
